title: ⚖️ Germany wants to criminalize publishing deepfakes... and up to 5 years in prison for sensitive personal content!
body: ⚖️ Germany wants to criminalize publishing deepfakes... and up to 5 years in prison for sensitive personal content!

Germany's Federal Council, the Bundesrat, is moving toward a firm stance against deepfake clips, proposing a law that criminalizes publishing fake AI-generated videos that look realistic to the point where they are hard to distinguish from reality.

The proposed law carries penalties ranging from fines to up to five years in prison in cases involving highly sensitive personal content, and the bill now moves to the Bundestag parliament for final deliberation, after the government acknowledged that current measures are not enough to face the spread of these polished clips.

The law targets both the makers and the publishers of fake clips, because it sees them as a threat to personal freedoms and to the democratic process itself, since a convincing fake video can be used to damage someone's reputation or mislead public opinion before anyone discovers it is fake.

The law could push tech companies and AI developers to improve tools for detecting fake content, while its supporters believe it could deter the making of fake clips in the short term, and shape global AI regulation in the long term.
Simply put: a fake video could land its maker in prison for five years... are laws alone enough to stop deepfakes?
Do you trust your ability to tell a real video from a fake one?
